title: 2025 AMC 8 Problem 11
statement: A tetromino consists of four squares connected along their edges. There are five possible tetromino shapes, \(\mathrm{I}\), \(\mathrm{O}\), \(\mathrm{L}\), \(\mathrm{T}\), and \(\mathrm{S}\), shown below, which can be rotated or flipped over. Three tetrominoes are used to completely cover a \(3 \times 4\) rectangle. At least one of the tiles is an \(\mathrm{S}\) tile. What are the other two tiles?
